name: How to Reverse Calculate Canadian GST/HST for Input Tax Credit (ITC) Claims
description: Step-by-step CRA guidelines to isolate GST/HST and calculate eligible Input Tax Credits from tax-inclusive Canadian invoices.

step.name: Identify the applicable provincial tax rate and structure
step.text: Determine if the purchase occurred in an HST province (Ontario 13%, Atlantic 15%), a GST-only province (Alberta 5%), or a dual GST+PST province (BC 12%).

step.name: Use statutory CRA ITC fractions or divisors
step.text: For 5% GST, multiply total by 5/105 or divide by 1.05. For 13% Ontario HST, multiply by 13/113 or divide by 1.13. For 15% Atlantic HST, multiply by 15/115 or divide by 1.15.

step.name: Separate deductible GST/HST from non-deductible provincial tax
step.text: In dual-tax provinces (BC, SK, MB), only the 5% GST portion qualifies for CRA Input Tax Credits; provincial PST is expensed as an operating cost.

step.name: Record pre-tax base and claimable ITC in your accounting ledger
step.text: Record the pre-tax amount as your net expense and the isolated GST/HST in your CRA Line 106/108 ITC reconciliation.

mainEntity.name: How do I calculate the price before HST in Ontario?

acceptedAnswer.text: Ontario's HST rate is 13%. Divide the HST-inclusive total by 1.13 to find the pre-tax price. Example: $226.00 / 1.13 = $200.00. The HST paid was $26.00.

mainEntity.name: How do I remove GST from a price in Alberta?

acceptedAnswer.text: Alberta charges only the federal 5% GST with no provincial sales tax. Divide your total by 1.05. Example: $105.00 / 1.05 = $100.00 pre-tax price.

mainEntity.name: What is the combined tax rate in Quebec?

acceptedAnswer.text: Quebec charges the 5% federal GST plus the 9.975% QST (Quebec Sales Tax) administered by Revenu Québec. Since 2013, QST is calculated directly on the selling price (not stacked on top of GST), creating a flat combined rate of 14.975%. Divide tax-inclusive receipts by 1.14975 to extract pre-tax amounts.

mainEntity.name: What is the difference between GST, HST, and PST in Canada?

acceptedAnswer.text: GST (Goods and Services Tax) is the federal Canadian tax at 5%, applicable in all provinces. HST (Harmonized Sales Tax) combines the federal GST with a provincial component into a single rate, used in Ontario (13%), New Brunswick (15%), Nova Scotia (15%), Newfoundland (15%), and PEI (15%). PST (Provincial Sales Tax) is a separate provincial tax charged alongside GST in British Columbia (7%), Saskatchewan (6%), and Manitoba (7%).

mainEntity.name: How do I reverse calculate GST/HST for an input tax credit claim?

acceptedAnswer.text: To claim an input tax credit (ITC) from the Canada Revenue Agency, you need the GST/HST component of a purchase. Use the reverse formula to find the pre-tax price, then subtract it from the total to get the exact tax paid. Example for Ontario HST: Total $565.00 / 1.13 = $500.00 pre-tax. HST component = $65.00. This $65.00 is your claimable ITC.

mainEntity.name: Which Canadian provinces have the highest combined sales tax?

acceptedAnswer.text: The Atlantic provinces have the highest combined rates. Nova Scotia, New Brunswick, Newfoundland and Labrador, and Prince Edward Island all have a 15% HST. Ontario's 13% HST is mid-range. Alberta remains the lowest with only the 5% federal GST and no provincial sales tax.
